correctness.rationale: The triangular quadratic ODE has an exact flow. Direct projected-map evaluation gives \(\mathcal F-\mathcal S=(-\delta Q_Su,hC_S(u))\) and \(\mathcal F-\mathcal H=(-\delta Q_Su,0)\); the first iteration at time slice 2 is exactly the residual difference evaluated at \(u=(1+\delta)\mathbf1\) and \(u=\mathbf1\). The squared norms and small-h ratio follow without discarded terms. The polynomial-time reduction at \(h=1\) maps minimum bisection threshold B exactly to squared-error threshold \(n/2+9B^2\), with NP membership; forest dynamic programming is proved by induction on rooted subtrees. CHECK.py independently passed 430 exact-rational tests and six balanced-projection comparisons. No finite test is used as the proof.

value.rationale: The projector-choice problem explicitly left open in the motivating parareal study can encode an NP-complete minimum-bisection instance even for a globally solvable polynomial flow, a zero-preserving order-p coarse solver and two slices. The exact error formula, connected-component zero-defect criterion, polynomial-time forest boundary, and divergent small-h ratio offer structural guidance on when projection selection is intrinsically combinatorial and when the modified variant avoids the cut penalty. This is not a routine numerical lookup or a generic textbook stability bound.
